title: Acute hepatitis etiologies and HAV versus HEV clinical profiles
guide: Acute hepatitis outcomes (recovery m/c), viral causes (HAV in children, HEV in adults), drug and toxin causes (paracetamol, yellow phosphorus, mushrooms), and the complete HAV versus HEV comparison table (Picornaviridae vs Hepeviridae, feco-oral spread, incubation 30 vs 40 days, cytopathic vs immune injury, cholestatic pruritus, and IgM serology).

title: HAV vs HEV outcomes, serological kinetics and ALF classification
guide: FHF risk (HAV 1 in 2 lakhs vs HEV 20% in pregnancy), 8 vs 12 week recovery, HAVRIX vaccine (2 doses 6-12 months apart), MELD score parameters, the 20-week serological curve with stool shedding and IgM/IgG kinetics, ALF definition (hepatitis + encephalopathy + INR >= 1.5 without prior disease), and hyperacute/acute/subacute onset categories.

title: ALF causes, idiosyncratic DILI and Paracetamol stages I–IV
guide: Paracetamol m/c in Europe, dose-dependent (>7.5 g/day) vs idiosyncratic drugs (single-dose rifampicin, carbamazepine, PTU), CYP2E1 zone 3 NAPQI generation with glutathione depletion, and the four clinical stages of paracetamol poisoning culminating in Stage III survival-determining failure.

title: Rumack-Matthew nomogram, King's College criteria and NAC protocol
guide: Rumack-Matthew nomogram risk lines, King's College poor prognosis criteria (pH < 7.25 after 24 hr OR triad of PT > 100 s / INR > 6.5, creatinine > 3.4 mg/dL / anuria, and grade 3-4 encephalopathy), charcoal hemoperfusion < 4 hr, three-bag IV N-acetylcysteine infusion protocol, and oral methionine.
